text.text_excerpt: Very quaint hotel only a couple blocks off Bourbon street that includes all the character of The French Quarter. Not sure where the original hotel ended the new(er) rooms were added but all rooms are named after a jazz musician. We visited on 8/18 thru 8/22/21 and had a great time. This is our second time in Nola and second time staying here- we like it! The building is old, the exteriors are old, but the rooms are freshened up and if you want 5 Star amenities- do yourself & go book a $400/night room at the Sheraton. This is OLD TOWN, this IS The French Quarter. We came for the old feel and that is exactly what we got. Being that Covid is on it's second 'up-swing' there was no continental...

Just got back from a 4 day stay at the lovely Hotel. St. Pierre. It is centrally located and walking distance to almost everything! Check in was a breeze but wasnt very friendly. We also had friends staying and the rooms were different, one was smaller but bigger bathroom, different A/C and heating units but no big deal, we just hung out in the courtyards. Every housekeeper we ran into were so nice and friendly. We did not receive stay over service one day which was not a big deal to us, hey, we work in the industry and understand these things can happen so they bought us towels. Stayed at Hotel St. Pierre for 7 days and loved it. This hotel is full of charm and it gives you a glimpse of what it was like living in one of the French styled homes. The location was perfect for us, far enough from the craziness and noise on Bourbon street but close enough for us to walk the streets and make it to bourbon or royal street. Yes the hallways are smaller and there are interesting pathways to other parts of the hotel that's what made this hotel interesting! This place was not originally built to be a hotel, it was a home at one point.
